resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Icelandic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Icelandic pass identified 25 actionable terminology, grammar, formula, and technical-clarity defects across electrical, circuit, TCR, trigonometric, thermal, SI, and wire-gauge content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Icelandic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The current definition repeated amperes in an ungrammatical phrase.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘amperum eða amperum’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to a concise definition of I measured in amperes.

findings.summary: The resistance bullet used the wrong grammatical gender.
evidence: The previous text began ‘Aukin viðnám’.

findings.summary: The voltage conclusion omitted the space before the unit.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended ‘5V’.

findings.summary: The electrical-power title used a general word for electricity rather than power.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Rafmagn’.

findings.summary: The electrical-power paragraph used literal terms for thermal capacity and safety margin.
evidence: The previous text used hitauppstreymi and loftrými.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with varmageta and öryggisbil.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating description mixed English loan wording with Icelandic grammar.
evidence: The previous description used ‘Joule hitun’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as Joule-upphitun and clarified energy conversion.

findings.summary: The Joule summary said current changes resistance into heat.
evidence: Electrical energy, not resistance, is converted into heat.
findings.resolution: Changed the summary to electrical energy converting into heat.

findings.summary: The constant-resistance bullet used the wrong adjective form.
evidence: The previous text said ‘Við stöðuga viðnám’.

findings.summary: The practical-safety paragraph used a literal word for safety margin.
evidence: The previous paragraph used loftrými in the margin sense.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with öryggisbil and clearer continuous-current wording.

findings.summary: The circuit-terms title used an awkward literal translation.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Hringrásarskilmálar’.

findings.summary: The circuit-terms introduction used an awkward phrase for interpreting a diagram.
evidence: The previous text said the terms made a diagram easier to reason about.
findings.resolution: Changed it to natural Icelandic wording about interpreting a circuit diagram.

findings.summary: The voltage-law title began with an unnecessary lowercase letter.
evidence: The previous title was ‘spennulögmál Kirchhoffs’.

findings.summary: The parallel-cell formula localized C_pack inconsistently.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘C_pakki’.

findings.summary: The power-balance bullet used an incorrect compound.
evidence: The previous bullet ended with ‘valdajafnvægi’.

findings.summary: The TCR description used metur rather than describing the coefficient.
evidence: The previous description said the coefficient ‘metur’ how resistance changes.

findings.summary: The TCR power paragraph had incorrect Icelandic word order.
evidence: The previous sentence said ‘hækkar hitastig eykur viðnám’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the constant-voltage and constant-current cases.

findings.summary: The right-triangle explanation used a wrong word for the hypotenuse and awkward ratios.
evidence: The previous text used undirstöng and literal ratio wording.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with undirstúka and clear Icelandic geometry wording.

findings.summary: The right-triangle formulas used inconsistent localized labels.
evidence: The previous expressions used mixed labels for opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard sin, cos, and tan formula labels.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity display name used a less precise compound.
evidence: The previous display name was ‘Hitageta’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux formula localized Q_dot into an invalid identifier.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘q'' = Q_punktur / A’.

findings.summary: The local-peak check used an infinitive instead of an instruction.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘Aðgreina’.

findings.summary: The final heat-flux check used an infinitive and imprecise heat-capacity term.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘nota hitagetu’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to an imperative and clarified varmageta.

findings.summary: The inch conversion formula used the plural noun for a singular value.
evidence: The previous expression began ‘1 tommur’.

findings.summary: The conversions paragraph mistranslated square inches as square meters.
evidence: The previous sentence used ‘fermetrar’ for square inches.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ferningstommur and rúmtommur.

findings.summary: The AWG paragraph used an ungrammatical word for current capacity.
evidence: The previous sentence used ‘afkastagetu’ with the wrong case and meaning.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with straumgeta and precise installation factors.
